primitives.name: Optimal Control Pace
primitives.verbatim_quote: Optimal control: maximize ∫v dt subject to dynamics, 0 ≤ f ≤ F, 0 ≤ E ≤ E0.
primitives.latex: \max_{f(t)} \int_0^T v(t) dt, \quad \text{s.t.} \quad \frac{dx}{dt}=v, \; 0\leq f\leq F, \; 0\leq E\leq E_0
primitives.assumptions: Dynamics governed by Newton's second law with gravity, drag, fatigue accumulation, and carbohydrate oxidation; force and energy bounded.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Bang-bang control with singular arcs when constraints are active; optimal pace switches between maximum force, singular velocity, and minimum energy.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's situational reasoning via state-transition models: athlete state = (velocity, energy, fatigue); controls = applied forces; constraints = physiological limits. Maps to GSI's conformal prediction via Hamiltonian Monte Carlo for posterior inference on optimal trajectories.
layer2.telemetry: Observed race velocity traces v(t) along with measured force f(t) and energy depletion E(t) from wearable sensors.

primitives.name: Fatigue Accumulation Rate
primitives.verbatim_quote: Hamiltonian with state-constraint penalty η; switching function ψ = ∂H/∂f = ιλ_v - χλ_E v + λ_Q v (linear in f → bang-bang + singular arcs).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'ι': 'Dimensionless Lagrange multiplier', 'χ': 'Dimensionless constant', 'λ_v': 'Adjoint variable for velocity (s/J)', 'λ_E': 'Adjoint variable for energy (1/J)', 'λ_Q': 'Adjoint variable for fatigue (1/J)', 'v': 'Velocity (m/s)'}
primitives.assumptions: Fatigue Q accumulates proportionally to work rate (f·v); adjoint equations derived from Pontryagin's minimum principle; state constraints handled via penalty method.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Switching occurs when ψ = 0; bang arcs correspond to extreme force values (f = 0 or f = F); singular arcs occur when ψ changes sign smoothly.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's state-transition framework where fatigue Q is a hidden state; the ODE dQ/dt = K·f·v updates Q based on observed forces and velocities. Maps to GSI's Bayesian inference via latent Gaussian processes where the switching function ψ identifies critical fatigue thresholds.
layer2.telemetry: Time series of accumulated fatigue Q estimated from force and velocity measurements; switching times identified from zero-crossings of ψ.

primitives.name: Singular Pace Arc
primitives.verbatim_quote: Theorem 1: optimal = maximal-force subarcs at start and on uphills steeper than α0, singular subarcs elsewhere; flat-route structure: max-force → interior arc → max-energy boundary arc (E≡1) → interior arc → depleted-energy arc (E≡0).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'v_s': 'Singular velocity (m/s)', 'σ': 'Aerobic supply (W)', 'Q': 'Fatigue (dimensionless)', 'K': 'Fatigue rate constant (1/s)', 'F': 'Maximum force (N)', 'α0': 'Critical slope angle (rad)'}
primitives.assumptions: On flat routes, singular arcs exist when energy constraint is inactive; uphill, singular arcs require steepness above a threshold α0; downhill, singular arcs may be infeasible.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Singular arcs occur when the switching function ψ vanishes identically; they represent a trade-off between maintaining high speed and conserving energy/fatigue.

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSE's situational reasoning via piecewise-deterministic Markov processes: singular arcs define regions of continuous control; transitions between arcs (e.g., max-force to singular) are discrete events modeled as jumps. Maps to GSI's conformal prediction via changepoint detection on velocity traces.
layer2.telemetry: Identifying singular arcs requires detecting intervals where acceleration \dot{v} ≈ 0 while energy E remains constant; this can be verified from accelerometer data.
